title: Rhymer

scenario.title: Sound-alike names for a new product
scenario.body: Feed in a brand name, get a list of sound-alikes to check. The book splits a word at its first a, e, i, o or u. That gives 'qake' instead of 'quake', turns 'queen' into 'bueen', gives up on 'éclair', and can't rhyme a name pasted with a space in front. Fix those without changing a single line the book's tests look at.

tagline: Give Rocky a word and he drops a whole verse of rhymes: he keeps the end of the word and swaps the sound at the front.

brain_blurbs.book: Chops the word at the first a, e, i, o or u.
brain_blurbs.real: Knows q comes with u, and that é is still a vowel.

rules.test_usage: Explains himself when you ask for help
rules.test_take: "take" gives 56 rhymes, from bake to zake
rules.test_chair: "chair" swaps the whole "ch": blair, fair, hair…
rules.test_apple: "apple" starts with a vowel, so every sound goes in front: 57 rhymes
rules.test_no_vowels: A word with no vowels can't be rhymed, and Rocky says so
rules.test_q_brings_its_u: Says "quake", never "qake": a Q always brings its U
rules.test_qu_is_one_sound: "queen" rhymes with green and screen, not "bueen"
rules.test_accented_vowels_are_vowels: "éclair" starts with a vowel too (é counts!)
rules.test_spaces_around_are_ignored: Extra spaces around the word don't matter
rules.test_never_rhymes_with_itself_or_repeats: Never repeats a rhyme, and never rhymes a word with itself
